items.title: Section: The Ground of the Hearer-Disciples Opens

items.zh: 如是已說修所成地。云何聲聞地？
items.en: Within the Basic Section, the thirteenth ground, the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples: the first yogic process, the chapter on the Ground of Spiritual Lineage. …Thus the Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation has already been explained. What is the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples?

items.zh: 一切聲聞地總嗢拕南曰：若略說此地，姓等數取趣，如應而安立世間、出世間。此地略有三：謂種姓、趣入、及出離想地。是說為聲聞。

items.title: The Ground of Spiritual Lineage Opens: What Is "Lineage"?

items.zh: 云何種姓地？謂嗢拕南曰：若略說一切種姓地，應知謂自性、安立、諸相、數取趣。謂若種姓自性、若種姓安立、若住種姓者所有諸相、若住種姓補特伽羅，如是一切總略為一，名種姓地。云何種姓？謂住種姓補特伽羅，有種子法。由現有故，安住種姓補特伽羅，若遇勝緣，便有堪任、便有勢力、於其涅槃能得能證。問：此種姓名有何差別？答：或名種子，或名為界，或名為性，是名差別。
items.en: What is the Ground of Spiritual Lineage? …Whether it is the intrinsic nature of spiritual lineage, or the establishment of spiritual lineage, or the marks possessed by one who abides in a lineage, or the persons who abide in a lineage — all of this together, in brief, is called the Ground of Spiritual Lineage. What is spiritual lineage? A person who abides in a lineage possesses the dharma of a seed. Because this seed presently exists, a person abiding in this lineage, upon meeting favourable conditions, thereby has the capacity, thereby has the power, to attain and to realise nirvāṇa. …Question: What distinctions exist among the names for this lineage? Answer: It is called, variously, a seed, a realm, or a nature — these are the distinctions.

items.title: The Essence of Lineage: A Seed Dormant in the Mind-Root Since Beginningless Time

items.zh: 問：今此種姓以何為體？答：附在所依，有如是相，六處所攝。從無始世展轉傳來，法爾所得。於此立有差別之名，所謂種姓、種子、界、性。是名種姓。
items.en: Question: What is the essence of this spiritual lineage? Answer: It is attached to its underlying basis, possessing marks such as these, comprised within the six sense-fields. It has come down, passed on from life to life, since beginningless time — it is obtained simply as things naturally are. Various distinguishing names are established for it: spiritual lineage, seed, realm, nature. This is called spiritual lineage. …Question: Should this lineage be said to belong to a single continuum, or to belong to many continua? Answer: It should be said to belong to a single continuum. …This seed does not possess distinct, differentiated marks across the six sense-fields.

items.title: Establishing Lineage: Subtle Before the Fruit, Coarse Once It Ripens

items.zh: 云何種姓安立？謂應問言：今此種姓，為當言細？為當言麁？應答言：細。何以故？由此種子未能與果、未習成果，故名為細。若已與果、已習成果，爾時種姓若種、若果，俱說名
items.en: What is the establishment of spiritual lineage? One should ask: should this lineage be called subtle, or should it be called coarse? One should answer: subtle. Why is this? Because this seed has not yet yielded its fruit, has not yet been cultivated to fruition, it is called subtle. If it has already yielded its fruit, has already been cultivated to fruition, then at that time both the lineage-as-seed and the lineage-as-fruit are called coarse.

items.zh: 麁。問：如是種姓，當言墮一相續？墮多相續？答：當言墮一相續。所以者何？若法異相，俱有而轉；見彼各別種種相續、種種流轉。如是種子，非於六處有別異相。

items.title: A Seed in Name Only: Not Found by Dissection, Known by Its Fruit

items.zh: 即於如是種類、分位、六處殊勝。從無始世展轉傳來，法爾所得，有如是想及以言說，謂為種姓、種子、界、性，是故當言墮一相續。
items.en: It is precisely with regard to this kind of being, this stage of abiding in lineage, this excellence belonging to the six sense-fields — transmitted from one moment to the next since beginningless time, obtained simply as things naturally are — that such a notion and such language arise: calling it spiritual lineage, seed, realm, or nature. It should therefore be said to belong to a single continuum.

items.title: Four Obstacles That Keep a Genuine Seed From Bearing Fruit

items.zh: 問：若住種姓補特伽羅有涅槃法，此住種姓有涅槃法補特伽羅，何因緣故有涅槃法，而前際來長時流轉，不般涅槃？答：四因緣故，不般涅槃。何等為四？一、生無暇故；二、放逸過故；三、邪解行故；四、有障過故。云何生無暇？謂如有一，生於邊國及以達須、蔑戾車中，四眾、賢良、正至、善士、不往遊涉。是名生無暇。
items.en: Question: If a person abiding in lineage possesses the dharma of nirvāṇa, why is it that this person, possessing the dharma of nirvāṇa, has nonetheless been cycling through a long span of time since the beginningless past, and has not yet attained nirvāṇa? Answer: Because of four causes and conditions, nirvāṇa is not attained. What are the four? Birth without leisure; the fault of heedlessness; wrongly-oriented conduct; and the fault of being obstructed. What is birth without leisure? It is like one who is born in a border region, or among the Daśyu or Mleccha peoples — places where the fourfold assembly, the virtuous, those who have arrived at the truth, and good persons do not travel or pass through. This is called birth without leisure.

items.title: Two More Obstacles: Heedless Comfort, and Wrong Views That Block Every Teacher

items.zh: 云何放逸過？謂如有一，雖生中國，或非達須、非蔑戾車，四眾、賢良、正至、善士皆往遊涉；而生貴家，財寶具足，於諸妙欲耽著受用，不見過患，不知出離。是名放逸過。云何邪解行？謂如有一，雖生中國，乃至廣說；而有外道種種惡見。謂起如是見，立如是論：無有施與，廣說乃至我自了知無諸後有。復由如是外道見故，不值諸佛出現世間，無諸善友說正法者，是名邪解行。
items.en: What is the fault of heedlessness? It is like one who, though born in a central land [where the Dharma is present] …is born into a wealthy family, possessing an abundance of riches, indulging attachment to fine sensory pleasures, seeing no fault in them, and knowing nothing of renouncing them. This is called the fault of heedlessness. What is wrongly-oriented conduct? It is like one who, though born in a central land, and so on as stated above, holds various wrong views of the non-Buddhist teachers. Such a one gives rise to views and establishes teachings such as: there is no such thing as giving — and so on at length, down to — I myself know that there is no further existence. Further, because of holding such non-Buddhist views, this person never encounters a buddha appearing in the world, nor any good friend who teaches the true Dharma. This is called wrongly-oriented conduct.

items.title: The Fourth Obstacle: Three Kinds of Genuine Obstruction, and the Monk Who Could Not Be Taught

items.zh: 云何有障過？謂如有一，雖生中國，廣說如前，亦值諸佛出現於世，遇諸善友說正法者；而性愚鈍，頑騃無知，又復瘖瘂，以手代言，無力能了善說、惡說所有法義；或復造作諸無間業。或復長時起諸煩惱。是名有障過。如是名為四種因緣。由此因緣故，雖有般涅槃法，而不般涅槃。
items.en: What is the fault of being obstructed? It is like one who, though born in a central land …is by nature dull-witted, stupid and ignorant, or further, mute — communicating only by gesture — lacking the capacity to understand the meaning of any teaching, well-spoken or ill-spoken. Or again, one who has committed one of the acts of immediate retribution. Or again, one who has, for a long time, given rise to the afflictions. This is called the fault of being obstructed. These, then, are the four causes and conditions. Because of these causes and conditions, even though the dharma for attaining nirvāṇa is present, nirvāṇa is not attained.

items.title: When the Obstacles Lift — and the Beings for Whom They Never Will

items.zh: 彼若值遇諸佛出世，聽聞正法，獲得隨順教授教誡，無彼因緣，爾時方能善根成熟，漸次乃至得般涅槃。無涅槃法補特伽羅，住決定聚。彼若遇緣、若不遇緣，遍一切種，畢竟不能得般涅槃。問：
items.en: If that person encounters a buddha appearing in the world, hears the true Dharma, and receives instruction and admonition in accordance with it — free of those obstructing causes and conditions — then, at that time, the roots of goodness are able to ripen, and one gradually proceeds, in time, to the attainment of nirvāṇa. …A person who lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa abides in the fixed group. Whether or not such a person encounters favourable conditions, in every possible circumstance, that person is ultimately unable to attain nirvāṇa.

blocks.text: Today begins the thirteenth stage, the **Śrāvaka Stage** (聲聞地), which runs through fascicle 34. It is the treatise's great manual of meditation for the "hearers", disciples who attain liberation by hearing the Buddha's teaching. Venerable Miào Jìng: "sound" (聲) here is the Buddha's words of Dharma. It opens with **spiritual lineage** (種姓, *gotra*): who has the capacity for liberation.

"A person who abides in a lineage possesses the dharma of a seed. Because this seed exists, upon meeting favourable conditions, one is able to attain nirvāṇa." Venerable Miào Jìng: lineage, seed, element, nature: different names, one meaning.

Where is the seed? It is "a distinctive feature of the six sense bases, continuing from beginningless time". Master Cháng Bǎi: wherever one is reborn, the mind faculty always exists, so the seed is carried there. Venerable Miào Jìng notes a difference between texts: the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* says the uncontaminated seed is formed later through hearing; this treatise says it is innate.

Before it bears fruit the seed is "subtle"; once it has, both seed and fruit are "coarse". It cannot be found by dissection, only known by its results. Master Cháng Bǎi: we say a good musician has "musical cells"; cut the body open, and where are they?

Even with the seed, nirvāṇa is not attained because of four obstacles: - **No leisure:** birth in a border region where the fourfold assembly and "those who have arrived" are absent. - **Heedlessness:** born rich and comfortable, one is carried along by pleasure. Master Cháng Bǎi: if merit exceeds wisdom, merit becomes an obstacle. - **Wrong conduct:** meeting other teachings and adopting their wrong views. - **Obstruction:** dullness, one of the five heinous deeds, or long-habituated affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: a headache is not a "karmic obstruction"; the term here means the heinous deeds.

subs.head: Those without the dharma of nirvāṇa

blocks.text: For a person who "lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa", conditions make no difference: such a person can attain good human and heavenly births, but not nirvāṇa. This is the controversial Yogācāra doctrine of beings "without lineage". Venerable Miào Jìng will warn later (Day 180) that we can never judge who such a person is.

quiz.q: What is the "sound" in "hearer," per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the Buddha's words of Dharma — heard from teachers and friends, leading to practise and realisation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the "sound" in the Ground of Hearers is the Buddha's words of Dharma. He adds that hearing, reflection, and cultivation are shared by all, while from the Ground of Hearers on the paths diverge; Master Cháng Bǎi likewise says they are common to the three vehicles.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define "spiritual lineage"?
options: a lineage-bearer has the dharma of a seed; because it presently exists, on meeting favourable conditions one has capacity and power to attain and realise nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "A person who abides in a lineage possesses the dharma of a seed. Because this seed presently exists… upon meeting favourable conditions, one has the capacity and power to attain and realise nirvāṇa." Venerable Miào Jìng: "presently" means not in the future; "exists" means not absent.

quiz.q: Lineage is also called seed, realm, and nature. What do the masters say distinguishes these names?
options: Miào Jìng: differences in name only, not meaning; Cháng Bǎi: "realm" means having the cause that will yield nirvāṇa
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: whether called lineage, seed, realm, or nature, the difference is only in name; the meaning is the same. Master Cháng Bǎi: "realm" refers to this kind of person possessing the cause that will later yield nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: What simile does Master Cháng Bǎi use for a seed that cannot be found yet truly exists?
options: "musical cells" — we say someone has them, but cutting the body open finds none
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if someone plays well, we say they have "musical cells" — but cut the body open, and where are they? Not found. The seed and conditioned things are neither identical nor separate; do not cling to a real seed.

quiz.q: Why does one with the dharma of nirvāṇa keep cycling without attaining it? Which four causes does the treatise give?
options: birth without leisure, heedlessness, wrong conduct, obstruction
quiz.why: "Because of four causes and conditions, nirvāṇa is not attained: birth without leisure; the fault of heedlessness; wrongly-oriented conduct; and the fault of being obstructed." Master Cháng Bǎi: though possessing the noble lineage, one still cannot achieve the path.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi clarify "karmic obstruction" is not?
options: not the casual expression — a headache is not a karmic obstruction but a resultant one
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "karmic obstruction" is not the everyday expression — a headache is not a karmic obstruction but a resultant obstruction. Here it means specifically the five acts of immediate retribution.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say of a person lacking the dharma of nirvāṇa?
options: abides in the fixed group; meeting conditions or not, in every circumstance, ultimately cannot attain nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "A person who lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa abides in the fixed group. Whether or not such a person encounters favourable conditions, in every possible circumstance, that person is ultimately unable to attain nirvāṇa." Venerable Miào Jìng: "every circumstance" means in heaven or among humans, anywhere in the three realms and five destinies — no way.
